content:
**sdd/issue-569-portreach-runtime-spy/explore**

## Exploration: issue #569 — verify SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH behaviourally (getVcs runtime spy)

### Current State

`brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs` dispatches four subcommands (memory-gate, decision-gate, issue-link, diff-size) and declares a self-authored manifest `SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH` (:453-458) claiming which handler reaches the VCS port (`getVcs`, imported at :74 from `../vcs/cli.mjs`). Only `issue-link: true`; the other three are `false`.

`run-check.test.mjs` T7 (:375) proves the manifest's KEY SET matches the actual dispatch (text-scan of `checkName === 'x'` branches). T7b (:392-819) is a much larger, purely TEXT-based scanner (`bodyClosure`/`crossFileClosure`, :514-583) that walks each handler's local call closure as a string, looking for `/\bgetVcs(Fn)?\b/`. Its own header comment (run-check.test.mjs:392-494) is a detailed changelog of FIVE previously-fixed "vacuous pass" routes (#535, #551) and explicitly documents a SIXTH, unclosed one — "ROUTE 6" (:465-480) — plus the still-open "NAME SHADOWING/COLLISION" residual (:444-454, tracked to #569): `bodyClosure` matches `function <name>(` by text with no scope analysis, so `crossFileClosure`'s tail call (:568) can resolve to a same-named LOCAL in the target module instead of the exported one — a confident WRONG answer, in either direction. The comment states plainly: "Until that lands [runtime spy], a resolved (non-null) closure from this scanner is not a guarantee the read is complete or correct."

Route 6's three shapes (from the maintainer scoping comment / PR #571 review, all still just NAMED in comments, none have a committed regression test):
1. transitively-called helper reached through an import the scanner can't follow (double-quoted/non-relative/dynamic/re-export-with-rename) — the `?? ''` accumulator fallback at the recursion site (:544) absorbs unresolvability at ANY depth, not just top-level.
2. an arrow-declared helper inside `checks/adr-presence.mjs` reached from decision-gate's own handler chain — getVcs() genuinely called at runtime, manifest stays `false`, suite stays green. NOTE: verified `checks/adr-presence.mjs` (read in full) has NO getVcs import/call today — this is a hypothetical reproduction shape, not existing production behavior; it must be built as a temp-file fixture, not found in real code.
3. dynamic-name sentinel: `const _n = 'get' + 'Vcs'; globalThis[_n]();` — nothing scans for string concatenation or dynamic property access.

`issue-link` already has a real seam: `defaultFetchIssue(ctx, { getVcs: getVcsFn = getVcs } = {})` (run-check.mjs:195-205), invoked as `deps.fetchIssue ?? defaultFetchIssue(ctx, deps)` (:358) — so `deps.getVcs` threads straight through. Confirmed exercised today by `run-check.test.mjs:917-932` ("defaultFetchIssue selects the provider from ctx.provider...") which passes `getVcs: async (opts) => {...}` directly as a runCheck dep. The other three handlers (`runMemoryGateCheck`, `adrPresence` dispatch, `runDiffSizeCheck`) have NO such seam and, per the checks/*.mjs source (memory-presence.mjs, adr-presence.mjs, diff-size.mjs all read — none import `getVcs` or `../vcs/cli.mjs`), have no organic reason to need one.

`getVcs` itself (`brain/scripts/vcs/cli.mjs:121-144`) is a plain named async export, not a singleton/cached instance — each call resolves the provider name then does a fresh dynamic `import(url)` of `./providers/${name}.mjs`, optionally wraps with `bindIdentity`. No default export, no module-level memoization to worry about for mocking.

`workflow-auth.mjs:187-199` (`parseSubcommandManifest`) reads `SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH` out of SOURCE TEXT (never imported, by design/D3) and returns `null` when the const's key/value regex matches ZERO pairs (D8, :198: `Object.keys(manifest).length ? manifest : null`). `workflow-auth.test.mjs` T4 (:324-336) only tests (a) empty source string → null, (b) the real 4-key manifest, (c) renaming the const → null. NO test constructs a manifest block that IS found (`start`/`end` resolve) but parses to zero key:value pairs — the exact D8 branch the issue calls out as uncovered. Per the issue, this test belongs in `workflow-auth.test.mjs` (co-located with `parseSubcommandManifest`), NOT `run-check.test.mjs` (avoids that file's first cross-subsystem import).

### Node/CI infrastructure findings (important gotchas)

- CI: `.github/workflows/release.yml:52` pins `node-version: '22'`. No `.nvmrc`, no `package.json` `engines` field in the repo — local Node version could not be verified in this session (no Bash tool available to this exploration agent); the apply phase MUST run `node --version` locally before relying on `mock.module()`.
- `package.json:58` test script: `"node --test \"brain/scripts/**/*.test.mjs\" \"test/**/*.e2e.test.mjs\""` — no flags, no `NODE_OPTIONS`, no `.npmrc` anywhere in the repo.
- Repo-wide grep for `mock.module` found ZERO existing usages — this would be the FIRST use of node:test's module-mocking API in this codebase.
- Web research confirms: `node:test`'s `mock.module()` / `t.mock.module()` requires the `--experimental-test-module-mocks` CLI flag (available since Node 22.3.0) and remains EXPERIMENTAL/unstable — no committed stability timeline. Two open upstream Node issues found: nodejs/node#53807 (module mocking confuses all future ESM imports into using CJS path resolution) and nodejs/node#55891 (`--experimental-test-module-mocks` not working as expected). This is a real adoption risk, not just a flag to add — needs local verification against whatever Node 22.x patch is actually installed in CI before committing to it.
- CRITICAL STRUCTURAL GOTCHA found during exploration: `run-check.test.mjs:18` already has a top-level STATIC `import { runCheck, main, SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH } from './run-check.mjs'`. Node's own mock.module() docs example explicitly requires the mocked module's consumer to be loaded via DYNAMIC `import()` AFTER `mock.module()`/`t.mock.module()` is called, precisely because ESM bindings are resolved at load time. Since `run-check.mjs` (and transitively `../vcs/cli.mjs`) is already statically imported at file-load time in `run-check.test.mjs`, calling `mock.module('../vcs/cli.mjs', ...)` inside a test in THAT SAME FILE would be too late — `run-check.mjs`'s `getVcs` reference is already bound to the real implementation. **The spy tests need their own NEW test file** that does NOT statically import `run-check.mjs`, and instead does `t.mock.module(...)` then `const { runCheck } = await import('./run-check.mjs')` inside each test body (or per-suite dynamic import after mocking).

### Affected Areas

- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs:74,195-205,453-458` — getVcs import, existing issue-link seam, the manifest itself (read-only reference point, likely unchanged by this issue).
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.test.mjs:392-819` — T7b's entire header comment + `bodyClosure`/`crossFileClosure`/`verifySubcommandPortReach` block; candidate for retirement/demotion once the spy lands (per issue's "Supersession" note). A NEW sibling test file (e.g. `run-check.port-reach-spy.test.mjs`) is the natural home for the spy suite, to avoid the static-import poisoning problem above.
- `brain/scripts/vcs/lib/workflow-auth.mjs:187-199` — `parseSubcommandManifest`, specifically the D8 branch at :198.
- `brain/scripts/vcs/lib/workflow-auth.test.mjs:322-336` (T4) — needs one new test for the empty-manifest-block case (e.g. `SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH = {\n};` with no pairs inside).
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/adr-presence.mjs` — confirmed NO existing getVcs reach; route-6 shape 2 must be built as a synthetic fixture (temp file), not asserted against the real file's current content.
- `brain/scripts/vcs/cli.mjs:121-144` — `getVcs`'s own shape (named export, fresh dynamic import per call) determines exactly what specifier string `mock.module()` must target (`'../vcs/cli.mjs'` as resolved from `run-check.mjs`'s own directory, or an absolute path — Node's mock.module resolves relative to the calling module).
- `package.json:58` (test script) — will need `--experimental-test-module-mocks` added, scoped ideally only to the new spy test file's invocation if node:test supports per-file flags, otherwise repo-wide via NODE_OPTIONS or the script itself.

### Approaches

1. **`mock.module()` global interception (issue-prescribed for the three seamless handlers)** — mock `../vcs/cli.mjs`'s `getVcs` export at the module-resolution level, dynamically re-import `run-check.mjs` after mocking, run each of the three handlers with a realistic fixture, assert the mock was never invoked (negative) or was invoked for the shadowing-fixture repro (acceptance criterion).
   - Pros: proves the NEGATIVE by execution, not text — closes route 6 (all three shapes) and the shadowing residual in one mechanism, independent of the scanner's vocabulary; matches the issue's own prescribed scope.
   - Cons: experimental flag (`--experimental-test-module-mocks`), unverified locally against installed Node in this session, two known open upstream bugs; forces a NEW test file (static-import poisoning above); adds CI flag surface.
   - Effort: Medium.

2. **Widen the `deps.getVcs` seam to all four handlers** — thread an injectable `getVcs` through `runMemoryGateCheck`/decision-gate's dispatch/`runDiffSizeCheck` the same way issue-link already has it.
   - Pros: zero Node-version/experimental risk, reuses an already-proven pattern, deterministic.
   - Cons: the issue itself states this explicitly — "Proving the NEGATIVE robustly needs global import interception, not a deps seam." A seam only proves "if this handler HAD been given a getVcs dep, would it call it" for the code path a developer remembered to thread — it does NOT prove that NO code reachable from that handler imports `getVcs` directly from `../vcs/cli.mjs` bypassing the seam (e.g., a future helper added deep in the call chain). Also speculative-generality smell: three handlers get a dependency they have zero organic need for, purely for testability.
   - Effort: Low, but does not satisfy the issue's acceptance criterion.

3. **Loader hook / `module.register()` custom loader interception** — intercept ESM resolution at a lower level than `mock.module()`.
   - Pros: conceptually similar power to option 1.
   - Cons: `module.register()` customization hooks are ALSO experimental in Node 22, add MORE moving parts (a separate loader file + registration boilerplate) for no clear benefit over `mock.module()`, which is node:test's own purpose-built answer to exactly this problem. Reinventing it is strictly higher effort for an equivalent risk profile.
   - Effort: High.

### Recommendation

Follow the issue's own prescription: Approach 1 (`mock.module()`) for the negative proof across `memory-gate`/`decision-gate`/`diff-size`, keep `issue-link`'s existing `deps.getVcs` seam UNCHANGED (already sufficient and already tested for the one case the manifest declares `true`). Do NOT widen the deps seam speculatively to the other three (Approach 2) — it cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion and adds unjustified surface.

Concretely:
- New test file (sibling to `run-check.test.mjs`, no static top-level import of `run-check.mjs`) housing the `mock.module()`-based spy suite. Each test: `t.mock.module('../vcs/cli.mjs', { namedExports: { getVcs: <spy fn> } })` → dynamic `await import('./run-check.mjs')` → invoke `runCheck(checkName, deps)` with a realistic fixture → assert spy call count.
- The acceptance-criterion fixture (shadowed name defeats the text scanner, spy answers correctly): construct two temp `.mjs` files — a "handler" module and a "target" module — where the target module has BOTH an exported function and a same-named local/nested function, arranged so `bodyClosure`'s `function <name>(` regex resolves the WRONG one (e.g., exported one calls `getVcs()`, a same-named local/shadowing declaration earlier in the same file does not, or vice versa) — run BOTH the existing text scanner (`bodyClosure`/`crossFileClosure`, imported or duplicated against the fixture) and the new spy against the SAME fixture, assert they disagree on this fixture and that the spy's answer matches the fixture's actual runtime behavior.
- Also build fixtures for route 6 shapes 1-3 (unresolvable import, arrow-helper-in-adr-presence-shape, dynamic globalThis lookup) as spy-proven negatives/positives, since the issue's scope explicitly names them.
- Add the D8 empty-manifest regression test to `workflow-auth.test.mjs` (near T4, :324-336): a `SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH = {\n};` block (found but zero pairs) must yield `null` from `parseSubcommandManifest`.
- Supersession decision (flag for sdd-propose/design, not resolved here): keep T7 (key-set symmetry — cheap, has no known residual, still useful even after the spy lands). Retire or clearly demote T7b's VALUE-checking closure walk (`bodyClosure`/`crossFileClosure`/`verifySubcommandPortReach` and their ~15 tests, :392-819) once the spy suite covers equivalent ground for all four subcommands, per the issue's explicit "should be retired or demoted, not kept as a second source of truth." Recommend demotion-then-removal in a follow-up slice rather than deleting in the same PR that lands the spy, to avoid a single PR both adding and removing large test surface (reviewability).
- MANDATORY pre-work before committing to `mock.module()`: verify installed Node version (`node --version`) against CI's pinned `'22'` and confirm `--experimental-test-module-mocks` actually works as expected on that exact version (nodejs/node#55891 suggests it may not, on some 22.x patches) — do this BEFORE writing the spy suite, as a spike/smoke test, since this determines whether Approach 1 is viable at all versus needing a fallback.

### Risks

- `mock.module()` is experimental and has two known open Node bugs; if it doesn't work reliably on the CI-pinned Node 22 (or the locally installed patch version), the whole spy approach needs a fallback — likely a scoped `module.register()` loader hook (Approach 3) as a worse-but-working substitute, adding real design cost. This must be spiked FIRST, not discovered mid-implementation.
- The static-import poisoning gotcha (run-check.test.mjs:18) is easy to miss; if the spy tests are added to the EXISTING `run-check.test.mjs` file instead of a new one, they will silently pass having verified nothing (mocking after the real binding is already resolved) — the exact "vacuous pass" failure mode this whole issue exists to close, recreated one level up in the new test infrastructure itself.
- Building believable, non-contrived fixtures for route 6 shape 2 (arrow-helper reached from decision-gate's real handler chain) risks either (a) not resembling anything that would ever really occur in `adr-presence.mjs`, weakening the fixture's persuasiveness, or (b) requiring an actual (contrived) modification to a temp copy of `adr-presence.mjs`'s shape — needs care to keep the fixture representative without asserting anything false about the CURRENT real file (which today has no getVcs reach at all).
- Test script (`package.json:58`) currently runs ALL `.test.mjs` files uniformly with no per-file flags; adding `--experimental-test-module-mocks` needs either a global flag addition (affecting every test file, low risk since it's additive) or a way to scope it — Node's test runner does not support per-file CLI flags within a single `node --test` invocation, so this will likely be a repo-wide addition to the `test` script, worth calling out explicitly in the proposal.
- Node engines/version pin is currently undeclared in `package.json` (no `engines` field, no `.nvmrc`) — this issue's fix effectively creates an implicit new minimum-Node requirement (22.3.0+ for `mock.module`) that should probably be made explicit at the same time, or at least flagged, since nothing else in the repo currently enforces it.

### Ready for Proposal

Yes. The exploration confirms the issue's own prescribed approach (mock.module for three handlers, existing seam untouched for issue-link) is sound and matches how `getVcs` is actually shaped (plain named export, fresh dynamic import per call — no singleton complications). The one thing sdd-propose/design must decide explicitly is the Node/mock.module() viability spike (must run BEFORE the design commits to this path) and the T7b supersession timing (same PR vs. follow-up slice).
